newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Traders see low offers in India diesel tenders.
newsitem.headline: Traders see low offers in India diesel tenders.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has received low offers for high speed diesel in both its term and spot purchase tenders for August delivery, traders said on Friday.
Despite the low offers, some traders said IOC was trying to get even lower premiums in its term tender for August 1997-March 1998 deliveries, to take advantage of the current soft market.
IOC was said to be keen to buy at between flat and a 10-cents premium to MidEast spot quotes, free-on-board (fob) basis, while the offers on an fob basis were at around 30-35 cents premiums.
Traders said while current prices are low, values would start to pick up by end August and September when regional buyers start to stock up for the winter months.
This explains the steep contango in the Singapore spot physical and swap markets, they said.
Traders said IOC would decide on its term tenders, which closed on July 2, and its spot tender which closed on July 3, later this evening.
IOC was expected to take up to 1.08 million tonnes of 1.0 and 0.5 percent sulphur diesel in its eight-month term tender, and around 450,000-550,000 tonnes in its spot tender.
In its last spot tender, IOC bought 855,000 tonnes for July delivery in 19 cargoes.
It also seeks one cargo per month of 0.25 percent sulphur diesel in its eight-month term tender.
Some of the low offers into the term diesel tenders are as follows (based on premiums per barrel to MidEast spot quotes): 1.0-percent suphur diesel:
Traders said offers into IOC's superior kerosene term import tender ranged between $2.00 and $2.30 per barrel above MidEast spot quotes, c-and-f Madras or Haldia on the east coast.
IOC also seeks one kerosene of cargo per month in its term tender.
Traders also said that offers into IOC's spot tender for August ranged between $1.70 and $2.00 per barrel above MidEast spot quotes, c-and-f Madras or Haldia.
Offers to Kandla on the west coast ranged between $1.00 and $1.30 per barrel above MidEast spot quotes, c-and-f basis, traders said.
